day_amj.title: Day surface temperature
day_amj.note: Ground, not air. Clear mornings around 11:25, April to June.
read: How hot the ground and the roofs get in the sun on clear mornings. The darker the orange, the hotter.

Before the rains the dry fields and bare ground around Kaolack heat up more than the town. After the rains the fields turn green and the town reads warmer than them, though some open ground in the south west stays hotter still. The salt flats along the Saloum read cooler than other bare ground in both seasons. So the hottest colour on a day map is often open ground, not the place where people suffer most, and these are not heat risk maps.
sure: About 2 °C over uniform ground, more over mixed roofs and streets. The real detail is about 100 m.
Where fewer than 10 clear images exist, cloud may be left in the colour. Dust in the air makes the satellite read the ground too cool, so on each morning the points under heavy dust are left out.
day_amj.box: This is the ground and the roofs. On a sunny morning a roof or bare ground can be 10 to 20 °C hotter than the air above it. It is not a heat risk map.
details: How hot the ground and the roofs get in the sun.
April to June, 2013 to 2026, Landsat 8 and 9.
About 2 °C over uniform ground, more over mixed roofs and streets. The real detail is about 100 m.
57 per point on average, from 3 to 128.

relative_amj.title: Relative to typical settled ground
relative_amj.note: Ground, not air. Clear mornings around 11:25, April to June.
read: Each place is compared with typical settled ground across the commune. Red runs warmer than a typical neighbourhood, blue runs cooler, white is about the same.
sure: The satellite cannot reliably tell apart differences under about 1 °C.
Colours fade where fewer than 10 clear images exist, since the colour says less there. The values are unchanged.
relative_amj.box: This is the ground and the roofs. On a sunny morning a roof or bare ground can be 10 to 20 °C hotter than the air above it. It is not a heat risk map.
details: All ground. Zero is the typical settled surface across the commune, so the map shows which places run hotter or cooler than typical settled ground.
April to June, 2013 to 2026, Landsat 8 and 9.
57 per point on average, from 3 to 128.

night_amj.title: Night surface temperature
night_amj.note: Ground, not air. Clear nights around 2:30, April to June. Real detail 1 km.
read: How warm the ground stays at night. The darker the orange, the warmer.
The river and the salt flats stay warmest at night. The town is under 1 °C warmer than the fields before the rains and about as warm as them after, a small difference at this scale.
sure: About 1 to 2 °C. The real detail is 1 km, so the map shows the river and the town against the fields, not single neighbourhoods.
Only clear nights count, and clear nights cool faster than cloudy ones, so read this map as a pattern rather than a typical night.
night_amj.box: This is the ground and the roofs at night, when they are closer to the air than by day. It is still not the air, and not a heat risk map.
details: How warm the ground stays at night.
April to June, 2013 to 2026, MODIS on the Aqua satellite.

type1.title: Riverbank
type1.note: Under 1% of the commune. Each point stands for about 100 m around it.
read: The kind of place at each point, from global land cover and urban climate maps: riverbank within 150 m of the Saloum, salt flats (bare ground or wetland within 600 m of water), fields and grass (grass, crops, trees), bare ground, and three kinds of settled ground (industrial, dense low rise, open low rise).
Each point stands for about 100 m around it, since a sensor speaks for its surroundings.
sure: We compared 15 random points of this type against high resolution satellite imagery. The type was right at 3 of them.
The check points on the map show where we looked.
details: ESA WorldCover and the global Local Climate Zone map (Demuzere and others, 2022).
